detailedExplanation: This topic is verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Biology Curriculum Outline 2026–27 and the corresponding AQA GCSE Biology 8461 content.
A stem cell is an undifferentiated cell that can divide to make more stem cells and can differentiate into other cell types.

Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into most types of human cell. Adult stem cells, for example those in bone marrow, can form a more limited range of cells such as blood cells. Plant meristems contain stem cells that can differentiate into any type of plant cell throughout the plant’s life.

Possible medical uses include replacing damaged cells in conditions such as diabetes or paralysis. In therapeutic cloning, an embryo can be produced with the same genes as the patient, reducing the risk that transplanted cells will be rejected.
Potential problems highlighted at this stage include transfer of viral infection and ethical or religious objections to the use of human embryos.
Plant meristem cells can clone plants quickly. This can preserve rare species or mass-produce crop plants with useful characteristics.
You must define stem cells, compare embryonic/adult/plant meristem stem cells and evaluate medical and ethical issues.
